title: Helical knitting for seamless stripes
subtitle: Working two yarns in a true spiral so stripes in the round have no jog at all.
excerpt: Helical knitting alternates two yarn colours in a genuine spiral, with each colour worked continuously around and around the tube. Because neither colour ever completes a full round, there is no point where one round ends and the next begins, and so the stripe is perfectly seamless with no jog to correct.
sourceNotes: Helical (or helix) knitting documented in modern knitting literature as an advanced method for eliminating the colour jog in striped circular knitting. Particularly associated with sock knitting. Standard technique published across UK and US knitting magazines and books.
heroPrompt: Close-up of a striped sock leg in two colours, the stripes running perfectly level around the tube with no visible jog or step at any point.

glossaryTerms.definition: A method of working two-colour stripes in the round by carrying both yarns simultaneously and alternating between them in a continuous spiral, so each colour works half the stitches of each round and no colour change jog appears.
The small visible step that appears at the start of each round when working stripes in the round, caused by knitting in a spiral rather than a true circle.

content.text: at its root by making the spiral nature of circular knitting work in favour of the pattern. Both yarns are always on the needles and alternate in use: colour A works a section of stitches, colour B picks up where colour A left off, and neither colour is ever dropped between rounds. Because neither colour completes a full round, there is no round boundary and no jog. The technique requires more attention than jogless stripes and is suited to knitters who are confident working in the round. Difficulty: advanced.
Fingering or DK yarn in two colours (colour A and colour B)
A circular needle or DPNs in the appropriate size
Two round markers in different colours to track each yarn's position
Cast on with colour A and work two full plain rounds in colour A.
At the start of the third round, work half the stitches with colour A and stop. Drop colour A and leave it hanging at the back of the work.
Join colour B at the point where colour A stopped and knit the remaining half of the round in colour B.
At the start of the next pass, colour A is waiting at the halfway point of the previous round. Pick it up and work the next half of the stitches in colour A.
When colour A reaches colour B's waiting position, drop A and pick up B to work the next set of stitches.

Continue in this way, each colour picking up just as the other is set down, maintaining the spiral. The stripe width in rounds is determined by how many rounds of each colour you work before switching to a new section width.

attrs.title: Tracking the yarns
attrs.body: Place a locking stitch marker on the needle at each colour's waiting position. Moving the marker forward as you work keeps you from losing track of where each yarn picks up. Some knitters prefer two distinctly coloured yarn bobbins so the colour labels match the yarn.

content.text: Helical knitting is most often used for sock legs and hat bodies where two-colour stripes must look flawless. It is also useful for seamless striped yokes. The technique works for any stripe width but is most commonly used for two-round and four-round stripes where the jogless method would still leave a visible step.

items.symptom: A ladder or gap appears where the two yarns meet
items.cause: Too much slack left in the yarn when picking up the waiting colour
items.fix: When picking up a waiting yarn, give it a firm tug before knitting the first stitch to close any gap. The first stitch after each colour pick-up is the critical one.

items.symptom: The two yarns are tangling around each other
items.cause: Both yarns are hanging on the same side of the work and twisting with each pass
items.fix: Drop each yarn on the opposite side of the work from the other. Untwist the yarns every few rounds by lifting the work and letting them dangle free.

items.cause: The yarn pick-up point drifted across rounds
items.fix: Use stitch markers to fix the handoff point for each colour at a consistent stitch position on every pass.
